title: Generative UI... in Python? — Jeremiah Lowin, Prefect
talk_summary: Jeremiah Lowin presents Prefab, a Python DSL that composes UIs from pre-built components into a serializable JSON intermediate representation, delivered as MCP apps so users interact with a real UI instead of routing everything through the agent's context window. The most transferable insight is that a compact intermediate representation (Python) streamed to an agent is ~70% smaller than the equivalent JSON, and that bypassing the agent for bulk data transfer avoids token waste.

takeaways.technique: Compact intermediate representation over verbose JSON
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of having the agent emit verbose JSON for a UI spec, they stream a more compact Python representation, execute it in a sandbox, and convert to JSON server-side.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the Python representation of a UI is about 70% smaller than the JSON representation. So we don't do this anymore.

takeaways.technique: Bypass agent context for bulk data transfer
takeaways.what_they_do: They route file uploads and large data directly from user to backend via a UI component, instead of forcing the agent to relay the bytes through its context window.

takeaways.technique: Serializable intermediate representation as the contract
takeaways.what_they_do: They made the JSON protocol the real product and the Python DSL a convenience layer, so the same representation can be generated by a human, an agent, or modified by an agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the key to this whole thing is the JSON in the middle ... because it's serializable, I can generate it from an agent. I can send it to an agent.

takeaways.technique: Ship a skill file so the agent can author the DSL
takeaways.what_they_do: They distribute a 'skill' describing how to write the UI DSL, so any agent can generate valid output without hand-defining each UI.
takeaways.evidence_quote: All you have to do is use the skill we already ship, share it with your agent so it knows how to write a UI
